task_instance: Diagnose why Run:ai workload 'training-job-42' in project 'ml-team' on a given cluster_id failed (user reports a possible OOMKilled / CrashLoopBackOff), producing the skill's read-only verdict: a root-cause category from the taxonomy, cited quantified evidence (phase, events, spec memory limit, pod k8sPhase, metrics peak), recurrence count over the lookback window, and a recommended next action.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a read-only live diagnosis that requires querying a running Run:ai cluster. Tier 1 needs the Run:ai MCP server tools (list_workloads, get_workload_status, get_workload_spec, get_workload_pods, get_workload_history, get_workload_metrics) with service-account read access; Tier 2 needs read-only Kubernetes credentials and the kubectl command (describe pod, logs --previous, get events, describe node). The office-assistant runtime grants only text file read/write/edit and web; it cannot invoke MCP tools (also disallowed by the safety rules), cannot run kubectl or any shell command, has no credentials, and there is no live cluster to inspect. There is no user-supplied document to analyze instead; the deliverable is derived entirely from live cluster signals that cannot be obtained here. Per the run rules I did not fabricate or stub the data these tools would return.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md at the skill path. It is explicit that Prerequisites are 'Tier 1 - MCP, required: service-account read access to workloads, submitted specs, pods, events, history, and metrics' and 'Tier 2 - Kubernetes, optional: separate read-only Kubernetes credentials'. The Tools table lists only MCP tools and kubectl invocations as the means to gather every signal (status, spec, pods, history, metrics, pod/node describe, previous logs, events). The classification in Step 5 must be driven by direct signals from those tools; the skill forbids classifying from the submit command or phase name alone and forbids manufacturing values. With no MCP tool access, no kubectl/shell, no Kubernetes credentials, and no live Run:ai cluster in this runtime, none of the required evidence can be collected, so no supported verdict can be produced or verified.
